principles: Prompt producers must not inject unbounded historical corpora into routine agent calls.
Removing an advisory content channel must not weaken signed lifecycle gates.
Regression evidence must measure the user-visible cost boundary.
drivers: Immediate prevention of multi-megabyte prompt expansion
Minimal code surface for a safe urgent fix
Compatibility with current structured story_review consumers

options.name: A: Delete corpus loading and concatenation now
pros: Eliminates the unbounded producer channel immediately
cons: Does not deliver the future CLI candidateSpecSet router

options.name: B: Keep reads and truncate the assembled prompt
cons: Silently drops documents by traversal order
Retains unnecessary filesystem and memory cost

options.name: C: Implement full M6 candidate routing in this Story
pros: Could provide richer targeted spec context
cons: Expands an urgent deletion into a large routing and process-fact change

chosen: A: Delete corpus loading and concatenation now
rationale: A directly removes the measured 2.5 MB producer-side cause while preserving the existing signed scope-check gate. B is unsound and C is intentionally deferred to the established M6 program.

preMortem.scenario: A leftover import or alternate code path still reads the corpus
preMortem.trigger: Only truthDocs.join is deleted while recursive traversal remains
preMortem.consequence: story_review still pays filesystem and memory cost
preMortem.mitigation: Static regression asserts no recursive requirements read/truthDocs channel and runtime test uses a large sentinel document

preMortem.scenario: Removing Truth Source accidentally removes structured PLAN content
preMortem.trigger: Prompt assembly is edited too broadly
preMortem.consequence: Reviewers lose understanding, decision, checklist, or verificationIntent context
preMortem.mitigation: Runtime regression asserts each preserved structured section and sentinel values remain

preMortem.trigger: Field is removed without checking structured-output tests
preMortem.mitigation: Inspect current consumers and preserve a truthful compatibility value only if necessary

preMortem.scenario: Token claim is exaggerated or not reproducible
preMortem.trigger: Only byte sizes or historical estimates are reported
preMortem.consequence: User cannot audit the savings claim
preMortem.mitigation: Record deterministic pre/post bytes and label token conversion as an estimate; separately report available host usage facts
